source: Anatomy: OpenKBP patient pt_14 (Babier et al., Med Phys 2021). The artifacts are simulated: polychromatic 120 kVp spectrum, NIST attenuation, Poisson noise, filtered backprojection.

items.label: Noise, exposure 1
items.cap: Poisson noise: the standard deviation of a uniform region rises as the exposure falls, as 1 / √(mAs).
items.facts: relative exposure 1: noise (SD in a soft-tissue region) = 19 HU

items.label: Noise, exposure 1/4
items.cap: Poisson noise: the standard deviation of a uniform region rises as the exposure falls, as 1 / √(mAs).
items.facts: relative exposure 1/4: noise (SD in a soft-tissue region) = 44 HU

items.label: Noise, exposure 1/16
items.cap: Poisson noise: the standard deviation of a uniform region rises as the exposure falls, as 1 / √(mAs).
items.facts: relative exposure 1/16: noise (SD in a soft-tissue region) = 75 HU

items.label: Sharp filter
items.cap: The ramp filter keeps the fine detail and the noise. The bone edges are crisp and the soft tissue is grainy.

items.label: Smooth filter
items.cap: A smoother filter averages neighbouring pixels. The noise falls and the fine detail softens.

items.label: Beam hardening
items.cap: The beam is polychromatic. The low-energy photons are removed first, so the beam hardens along thick paths and the centre reads lower than the periphery (cupping). Dark bands can also appear between dense objects. A softer beam, as here, hardens more.
items.facts: soft tissue: the centre reads -46 HU relative to the periphery (cupping)

items.label: Metal streaks
items.cap: A dense metal object (steel-like, 6 mm, illustrative) absorbs most of the beam along some rays. Those rays carry too few photons and are strongly hardened, so bright and dark streaks run between the object and other dense structures.
items.facts: streaks: the soft tissue away from the metal varies by 96 HU (SD) around the reference

items.label: Ring
items.cap: A group of three detector channels reads 5% high at every angle. The error is at the same distance from the centre of rotation in every projection, so it reconstructs as a ring.
items.facts: faulty or miscalibrated detector channels: a ring centred on the rotation axis

items.label: Motion
items.cap: The patient moves 6 mm during the scan, so the projections from the second half of the rotation no longer agree with those from the first half. Edges are doubled and streaks appear.
items.facts: the patient moves 6 mm half way through the rotation

items.label: Scatter (CBCT)
items.cap: Scattered photons add a smooth background to every projection. It is larger behind thick parts of the patient, so the attenuation is underestimated there. The centre looks less dense, and the HU are no longer accurate.
items.facts: soft tissue: the centre reads -122 HU relative to the periphery (cupping)
